answer: A Sybil-resistant registry can require every agent to stake a refundable bond and present a cipher-signed attestation from a unique hardware enclave before it can trade. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of bonds and distinct devices, while an agent caught double-signing loses its stake. That bond is the basalt layer under the market: hard and expensive to duplicate at scale, and ferrous in how it binds each identity to one real, accountable key rather than to a free username.
